Signed public Microsoft Windows Update trust-list samples were retrieved on 2026-10-08 from the endpoints documented in [Microsoft's CTL update documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-cs/certificate-trust). Microsoft's [disconnected distribution guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-cs/configure-trusted-roots-disallowed-certificates) describes copying these lists through local file/web servers. These files contain public certificate trust metadata, no private keys or executable payloads. Their origin is Microsoft. An explicit redistribution license for package inclusion has not been established, so the binary samples are excluded from the repository and crate package.

Only this audit README and provenance.json are retained here. Exact CTL bytes, CAB archives and separately downloaded bootstrap material remain in /data/cache/signcode-ctl-audit. Ignored tests/microsoft_ctl.rs reads fixed filenames from the explicitly configured SIGNCODE_MICROSOFT_CTL_FIXTURES directory; normal tests do not download anything. Extraction used Rust ms-cabinet 0.1.2 with 2 MiB input, 16 members, and 4 MiB aggregate decompressed bounds. Actual CABs each contain one MSZIP member; member paths were never used as extraction paths.

AuthRoot has 562 entries with 20-byte SHA-1 subject identifiers, list usage 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.9 and thisUpdate 2026-08-25. Attributes, including unknown policy OIDs, remain exact DER. Disallowed has 88 entries without optional attributes, list usage 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.30 and thisUpdate 2025-09-05. Its subject algorithm is Microsoft OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.11.15; identifiers comprise 82 values of 16 bytes and six values of 48 bytes. The parser preserves these values without assuming a conventional certificate fingerprint. Matching these identifiers requires a dedicated tested Windows adapter; parsing does not establish distrust enforcement.

Both embedded signers have root-list signer EKU 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.9. Both CMS cryptographic signatures pass the portable verifier with SHA-1 signatures disabled and independently pass OpenSSL 3.5.8 smime verification. AuthRoot's issuer is Microsoft Certificate List CA 2024; Disallowed's issuer is Microsoft Certificate List CA 2011. Both chains terminate at Microsoft Root Certificate Authority 2010.

The bootstrap root is independently provisioned from Microsoft's HTTPS [PKI repository](https://www.microsoft.com/pkiops/docs/repository.htm), which publishes SHA-1 thumbprint 3B1EFD3A66EA28B16697394703A72CA340A05BD5. Its SHA-256 is df545bf919a2439c36983b54cdfc903dfa4f37d3996d8d84b4c31eec6f3c163e, matching the already retained microsoft-ber-certificates/microsoft-root-2010.der fixture. The root is never derived from the downloaded list or automatically installed into trust.

AuthRoot authenticates at the pinned retrieval time. The downloaded Disallowed signer expires on 2026-03-28, so current-time authentication correctly fails even under a deliberately generous freshness bound. Tests authenticate that fixture at its historical thisUpdate and separately require current-time rejection. Historical success does not establish a current acceptable Disallowed snapshot. Authenticated-list objects do not yet interpret AuthRoot restrictions or implement Disallowed matching. These fixtures establish parsing and bootstrap checks, not complete Windows policy equivalence or certutil interoperability.
